title: task view has no field/note projection; returns all implementationNotes unbounded
description:
Raised by opum-agent (2026-09-13, durable copy OPAG-120) from a live proof-graph inspection: a research task on that probe already exceeds a million characters of implementationNotes, so a plain task view means loading a history nobody asked for. quest help task view advertises no projection or note-selection flags today -- a caller always gets the full record.

Proposed shape (opum-agent's framing, not settled here): select which top-level fields come back; fetch only the latest notes, or notes since a stable cursor; retrieve one complete note by a stable id/digest when the full text is actually needed (e.g. for proof evidence); and an explicit hard output budget whose response carries omitted-record/field metadata so a caller can tell truncation from completeness. The constraint opum-agent flagged as worth keeping: a bounded view must not become the ONLY way to read a note -- an exact, unbounded read needs to stay available.

Companion finding on the Lore side already sent to lore-cli (its context can retain a target larger than maxTokens while marking the result truncated) -- neither half fixes the other; this task is Quest's half only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest task view supports selecting a subset of top-level fields in its output
quest task view supports retrieving only the latest N implementationNotes, or notes since a given cursor, without fetching the full array
a single implementationNote can be retrieved in full by a stable id/digest independent of any bounded/paginated view
a bounded/paginated task view response carries metadata indicating what was omitted (which fields, how many notes), so truncation is distinguishable from completeness
an unbounded exact-read path remains available and documented for evidence use, not removed in favor of the bounded default
